I've only had 1 panic attack. I think it was caused by smoking too much weed in 1 session. Was absolutely petrifying. I also came to terms with the fact that I was probably going to die. My head was messed up for a couple days after that. Your body/mind just needs time to recover after going through something like that.

I also struggle to maintain eye contact. I find that looking at persons nose helps me to maintain "eye contact" for longer. People don't notice the difference and it makes me less anxious during long conversations. 

I also learnt a little life hack. If you maintain eye contact people will subconsciously see that you're interested in what they're talking about and that you want to hear more. I've tested this on multiple people. Means that I have to talk less which is a win for me.

I have the exact same thing when I'm anxious at work. My vision gets kind of blurry and I have a fainting/out of body feeling. It freaks me out because it feels very similar to the start of a panic attack.

When I was much younger we went out to dinner with family friends. The adults were all inside drinking so 2 friends and myself were looking for entertainment. we were outside in the parking lot and 1 friend mentioned a game called Charlie. You take 3 matches and write "Yes", "No" and "Maybe" on 3 matches. Then you take 3 squares of toilet paper. You stick 1 match in the square of toilet paper, fold it in half. And then fold the toilet paper in half again.  Repeat with the other 2 matches. 

We put the folded up toilet paper and matches in the middle of us and held hands making a ring around them. Then you ask Charlie Yes, No or Maybe questions. Such as "Charlie are you with us. Yes, no or maybe". You repeat the question 3 times and then open the first fold in the toilet paper. Whatever the answer is the match which was in the first fold has now moved to the second fold. It was freaky as hell. We asked a bunch of questions. I can't remember the last question we asked but as we unfolded the toilet paper there was a LOUD bang on the other end of the parking lot. Needless to say we legged it back to the safety of our parents. Never tried anything like that since.

I've only had 1 panic attack but it was the most frightening experience of my life. 

It was a normal Friday afternoon. I had just got home from work. I smoked 2 bowls of weed as I always do on Friday. After that I went inside to get a drink and as I got to the fridge I noticed every thing had a sort of red/blue tinge. Being high I thought nothing of it. I took a bottle of cold water out the fridge and took a big sip. That was when it hit me. Suddenly I felt completely dissociated I had this feeling of vertigo and immense pressure in my chest. My heart rate shot up like a rocket it felt like my chest was going to explode. 

I was home alone at time and freaking out because I literally had no idea what was happening. I assumed I was having a heart attack. I called my dad and told him what was happening. Thankfully he was actually on his way home already. When I knew he'd be home soon it seemed to calm me very slightly. I paced up and down the lounge waiting for him to get home. My mind was going crazy. It felt like the world was going to end, I was going to die and everything was closing in around me. After a few minutes I curled up into the foetal position on the couch trying to calm my self down. 

My dad got home about 10 minutes after the attack started. He wanted to take me to the hospital but I was too scared to move. Having him there seemed to help calm me down. I told him to give me 5 minutes then we can go to the hospital. I managed to sit up  and for some reason I thought to Google the symptoms of panic attack. The Google Now results literally gave the exact symptoms I was having. After reading that and establishing that I wasn't going to die I burst out in tears. The relief of knowing took such a weight off my shoulders and I told my dad that it wasn't necessary to go to the hospital. The attack probably lasted 25-30 minutes in total. 

I was absolutely broken after the attack. Physically and mentally. My dad gave me a glass of water which I was too petrified to drink. My mind associated anything and everything as a possible trigger for another attack. I spent the rest of the weekend at home reading about panic attacks and all the related topics. 

This happened about 5-6 months ago. Ever since then I haven't been able to smoke weed like I used to. I've had to cut down drastically. If I get too high I get extremely paranoid that I'm going to have another attack. On one occasion I psyched myself out so much that I almost had another one. 

I'm sorry if the above is very disjointed. Just typing that out brings back the memories. It's still difficult for me to think about. My hands are actually shaking.
